read: Read text lines or an image. Paths are relative to the launch directory. offset starts at 1; limit bounds lines. Follow next_offset when truncated.
bash: Run Bash in the working directory; returns output and exit code. timeout is seconds. Inspect state before retrying an interrupted command.
spawn_researcher: Delegate a web research question to a read-only researcher sub-agent (same model, own context, web search and page reading only). Use for fresh, external or multi-source facts: current events, versions, prices, laws and standards, source comparisons, background for a course or document. Not for ordinary conversation, explanations from your own knowledge, one quick lookup (use web_search/web_read) or anything about files. One researcher at a time; takes tens of seconds to minutes. It starts blank and sees only `question` and `context`, not the chat, notes, files or memory: put in everything it needs (exact subject, constraints, learner level and goal, what is known or excluded, time frame) and make the question self-contained. It returns JSON: summary, key_findings (claim + source ids), sources (id, title, url, note), open_questions, confidence low|medium|high (plus a report with [n] citations when output=report). Check confidence and open_questions, answer in your own words with the sources you rely on as links or a short list; never paste the raw JSON or claim more certainty than the result supports.

context.description: Why it is asked, the learner's level or goal, what is already known or must be excluded.

depth.description: quick: 1-3 sources; standard (default): about 3-6; deep: broad cross-checking.

output.description: brief (default): short summary and findings; report: also a markdown report with [n] citations.

language.description: Language of the result; default Russian.
